coverage: Read fully: server/routes.ts 2265-4527 (tail of PUT /orders/:id/items, PUT /orders/:id, payment, payment-method, settle-due, dues/tabs, payment-summary, bill-requested, hold/recall/cancel/move/merge/split, KOT, delivery webhook, reports, automation, CRM, staff/attendance/leaves/shifts/payroll); server/seed.ts 1-92; server/selfScope.ts 1-32; server/serverTiming.ts 1-55; server/services/aiMessageService.ts 1-195; server/services/auditService.ts 1-182; server/services/automationStore.ts 1-299; server/services/backupService.ts 1-144; server/services/birthdayService.ts 1-203; server/services/couponService.ts 1-321. Cross-checked callees: storage.getAttendance/getLeaves/mergeOrders/settleOrderIfUnpaid/getOrdersCollectedBetween/upsertStaffProfile, shared/settlement.ts, shared/orderMutation.ts, shared/orderPricing.computeTotals, whatsappService.sendWhatsAppMessage, automationRuleEngine.runAutomationServerSide, client Orders.tsx status select and POS.tsx move/merge. Earlier lines of PUT /orders/:id/items (before 2265) belong to another slice and were not reviewed.

findings.title: GET /api/attendance and GET /api/leaves (requireAuth) return full users/staffMembers rows incl. plaintext PINs, password hash and totpSecret
findings.detail: These routes return storage.getAttendance()/getLeaves() verbatim. Both (storage.ts ~1772 and ~1843) attach `user: userMap.get(...)` (SELECT * FROM users: password, pin, totpSecret) and `staffMember` (SELECT * FROM staff_members: pin) to every row. GET /api/attendance (any userId filter or none), /api/attendance/today, /api/attendance/me, /api/attendance/person and GET /api/leaves (all leaves, any person) are reachable by any logged-in session, including a bare staff PIN-card session. No sanitizeUser() is applied (CLAUDE.md's selfScope rule).
findings.failure_scenario: A staff-tier PIN session calls GET /api/leaves or GET /api/attendance (no filters). The JSON contains every manager's `user.pin` in plaintext. The staff member replays it to POST /api/auth/verify-pin {requiredRole:'manager'}, gets a 90s elevation grant (and requireFreshPin approval), and can cancel orders, write off bills, settle dues, apply discounts — exactly the escalation chain CLAUDE.md documents for the old /api/auth/profile leak.
findings.suggested_fix: Never embed raw user/staff rows: in getAttendance/getLeaves map to {id, username/name, role, designation} only (or run sanitizeUser and strip staffMember.pin). Additionally gate GET /api/attendance (unscoped) and GET /api/leaves (all people) behind requireManagerOrAdmin, keeping /me self-scoped.
findings.reason: storage.getAttendance/getLeaves (storage.ts 1772-1866) do SELECT * from users and staff_members and spread the full row as `user`/`staffMember` into every result; GET /api/attendance, /api/attendance/today and GET /api/leaves (routes.ts 4164-4180, 4401) are requireAuth only and res.json the result with no sanitizeUser. users.pin and staff_members.pin are plaintext columns (schema.ts 11, 870). Any leave/attendance row for a manager therefore ships that manager's PIN to a staff-tier session, which verify-pin turns into an elevation grant.

findings.title: PUT /api/orders/:id lets any session set status to 'cancelled' (or un-cancel / reopen a paid order) with no elevation, reason, audit or side effects
findings.detail: orderUpdateAllowlist permits `status` with any string. The route applies it with requireAuth only and no state checks. Orders.tsx disables the 'cancelled' item in its select, but that is UX only; it also freely allows picking 'pending'/'preparing' on a cancelled or paid order. The guarded cancel path (requireElevation('manager') + reason + inventory reversal + KOT completion + order.cancel audit) is fully bypassed.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) A staff session (or curl with its cookie) sends PUT /api/orders/123 {status:'cancelled'} on a paid order: it disappears from Total Sales/Top Items with no manager PIN and no audit row, while the cash stays in the drawer. (b) On Order History a staff member picks 'pending' on a cancelled order: it re-enters sales (status <> 'cancelled') and Live View's active orders, stock is not re-deducted, nothing is audited.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict `status` in the allowlist to a forward-only kitchen set (preparing/ready/served/delivered), reject 'cancelled' and 'hold' (use the dedicated routes), refuse any change when the order is cancelled or paymentStatus='paid' (409), and log an audit row for status changes.
findings.reason: orderUpdateAllowlist picks status with no value restriction (shared/orderMutation.ts) and PUT /api/orders/:id applies it with requireAuth only. Orders.tsx disables only the 'cancelled' option, so a staff member can move a cancelled or paid order back to pending/preparing from the UI, and a direct call can set 'cancelled' with no elevation, reason, inventory reversal or audit.

findings.title: PUT /api/kot/:id flips the parent order to ready/preparing unconditionally — resurrects cancelled orders and pulls served/paid orders back to active
findings.detail: When a ticket is set to 'completed' the route does updateOrder(orderId,{status:'ready'}); 'in-progress' sets 'preparing'. There is no check of the order's current status/paymentStatus, of the ticket's previous status, or of other tickets on the same order. Settle and cancel auto-complete tickets, but the Kitchen screen can be stale (15s poll/realtime gap) and the status value is not validated.
findings.failure_scenario: An order is cancelled (status 'cancelled', tickets completed). The kitchen tablet still shows the old ticket and the cook taps 'Mark Ready': the route sets the order to 'ready', so the cancelled order is now counted in Total Sales, Top Items and Live View 'Active Orders'. Same for a settled order (served -> ready): it reappears as an active floor order the day after.
findings.suggested_fix: Only advance the order when it is not cancelled and not already served/paid (conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status IN ('pending','preparing')), validate `status` against the KOT enum, and set 'ready' only when all tickets of the order are completed.
findings.reason: PUT /api/kot/:id (routes.ts 3459-3481) sets the parent order to ready/preparing unconditionally, with no check of the order's status or payment state and no validation of `status`. The defect is real. It is downgraded because it needs a Kitchen screen showing a stale ticket for an order that was already settled or cancelled, since settle and cancel auto-complete the tickets.

findings.title: POST /api/crm/automation/run is requireAuth, defaults to force:true and takes an unbounded client `limit` — any staff session can fire a real outbound WhatsApp/SMS batch
findings.detail: runAutomationServerSide({force:true, limit}) bypasses config.enabled and sends real messages through WATI/Meta/MSG91 (automationRuleEngine.ts). CLAUDE.md made the equivalent POST /api/automation/run requireAdmin precisely because a force-run is a real send batch and a ban-risk surface; this sibling route was left at requireAuth, and `limit` overrides maxPerRun with no cap.
findings.failure_scenario: A staff PIN session POSTs /api/crm/automation/run {limit:10000}: the server sends win-back/at-risk messages to every eligible customer even though the owner left automation disabled, risking a WhatsApp number ban and spamming customers.
findings.suggested_fix: requireAdmin on this route, default force to false, and clamp limit to config.maxPerRun.
findings.reason: POST /api/crm/automation/run (routes.ts 4067) is requireAuth and calls runAutomationServerSide({force: force ?? true, limit}). In automationRuleEngine.ts:299 force bypasses config.enabled, and at :318 the client limit replaces maxPerRun with no clamp. The sibling /api/automation/run is requireAdmin for exactly this reason, per CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: Merge does not reject targetOrderId === sourceOrderId or non-running orders — merging an order into itself deletes it
findings.detail: No equality or status checks. With equal ids, storage.mergeOrders inserts copies of the order's own items, then `DELETE FROM order_items WHERE order_id = source` and `DELETE FROM orders WHERE id = source` — removing the very order it just updated, all inside one committed transaction. Likewise a paid/cancelled source is deleted outright (losing a payment record), and a paid target gets its total raised after payment. The client excludes only `t.id !== preselectedTableId` from the source list, so a stale/mis-attached table row (table.currentOrderId pointing at the active order) or a direct call reaches it.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager taps a running table whose currentOrderId equals the order open in POS (e.g. a table left pointing at the order after a move/shift failure). The order and all its items are permanently deleted and the response is {success:true}; the KOT tickets are orphaned.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 400 when Number(targetOrderId) === Number(sourceOrderId); require both orders to be status not in ('cancelled','served') and paymentStatus='pending' (re-checked inside the transaction with a conditional UPDATE/DELETE).
findings.reason: The merge route (routes.ts 3253-3325) has no target!==source check and no status/paymentStatus check. With equal ids, storage.mergeOrders (storage.ts 1140-1164) inserts copies of the order's own items, then deletes every order_items row for that id and the order row itself, in one committed transaction. The defect is real. It is downgraded to medium because it needs a manager PIN, and the client excludes the current table, so it is reached only through stale or mismatched table state or a direct call.

findings.title: `npm run seed` hard-deletes menu_items, categories and inventory on the one shared production DB, with no guard or transaction
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md lists `npm run seed` as a normal command and states DATABASE_URL is the single shared production database. seedDatabase() unconditionally runs db.delete(menuItems)/categories/inventory, and also executes at import time (top-level call). Menu rows are deliberately never hard-deleted elsewhere because order history, reprints and reports resolve item names/categories by menuItemId.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer follows the Commands section and runs `npm run seed`: the live restaurant menu, categories and stock are wiped and replaced with 22 demo dishes; every historical KOT/bill reprint of a menu item now prints 'Item', category revenue collapses to 'Uncategorized', and stock_movements reference missing inventory (or the inventory delete fails midway, leaving a half-seeded DB since nothing is transactional).
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse to run unless an explicit flag/env (e.g. SEED_CONFIRM=<db name>) is set and the menu table is empty; wrap in a transaction; never delete menu_items (soft-delete or skip if rows exist); remove the top-level auto-run when imported.
findings.reason: server/seed.ts unconditionally runs db.delete on menuItems, categories and inventory with no transaction and no guard, and calls itself at top level. package.json's `seed` script runs it through dotenv against DATABASE_URL, which CLAUDE.md says is the single shared production DB, and CLAUDE.md lists `npm run seed` as a normal command.

findings.title: Cancel has no paymentStatus/status check and no conditional write — a paid order can be cancelled (and a concurrent settle overwritten)
findings.detail: The route reads the order, then storage.updateOrder(id,{status:'cancelled'}) unconditionally. A settled order can be cancelled; a settle landing between the read and the write is overwritten; a second cancel re-logs order.cancel. getOrdersCollectedBetween (Reports -> Payments) filters only paymentStatus='paid', not status, so the cancelled-but-paid order still counts as collected cash while /api/reports/sales excludes it.
findings.failure_scenario: A manager cancels a pickup order that was settled for ₹500 cash minutes earlier (Actions menu offers Cancel for pickup/delivery). Sales drops by ₹500 but Payments still shows the ₹500 cash, and inventory is restored for food that was served; Reports' two tabs disagree. A double-tap logs two 'Cancelled' KOT events.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the update conditional (WHERE status <> 'cancelled' AND payment_status = 'pending') and 409 otherwise (a refund of a paid order should be its own audited flow); skip duplicate audit when nothing changed.
findings.reason: The cancel route (routes.ts 3125-3174) reads the order, then calls updateOrder({status:'cancelled'}) with no check of paymentStatus or current status and no conditional WHERE. A paid order can be cancelled, which also restores its stock, and a repeat cancel logs order.cancel again. This is not one of the documented known gaps (that gap covers only the unconditional table free).

findings.title: Payment route frees order.tableId even when settling an old due whose table now belongs to another running order
findings.detail: freeTable() runs for every successful settle. A due order keeps its tableId after the first (due) settle freed the table. When that due is later settled through this route (Billing 'Mark as Paid' on the unpaid backlog, or the legacy flow CLAUDE.md says still works), updateTableStatus(tableId,'free',null) wipes whatever order currently occupies that table. CLAUDE.md lists this unconditional-free bug only for cancel and move-table; this third site is not documented.
findings.failure_scenario: Yesterday's table 4 bill was marked Due. Tonight table 4 is running a new order. The cashier settles yesterday's due from Billing: table 4 flips to 'free' with currentOrderId null, the running order vanishes from the Tables page and the next party is seated on it.
findings.suggested_fix: Free the table only if tables.currentOrderId = this order id (conditional UPDATE), or skip freeTable when the order was already served (a due being cleared).
findings.reason: freeTable in the payment route (routes.ts ~2716) frees order.tableId on every successful settle. A due order keeps its tableId, and Billing's Mark as Paid settles a served/pending due through this route, so the table's current running order is wiped. CLAUDE.md's known-bug note lists only cancel and move-table, so this third site is not documented.

findings.title: Loyalty points, settlement WhatsApp and feedback scheduling are fire-and-forget before res.json on Vercel
findings.detail: earnPointsForOrder, triggerSettlementMessage, triggerDueBillMessage and scheduleFeedbackForOrder are started with .catch() and never awaited; the response is sent immediately. CLAUDE.md documents that Vercel can freeze the function after the response (the reason audit rows are now awaited). The settle guard means these never re-run.
findings.failure_scenario: A customer settles a paid bill on the Vercel deployment; the function is frozen right after res.json and earnPointsForOrder's insert never runs. The customer's loyalty balance silently misses the points (later redeemable money), and the welcome/thank-you message is never enqueued — with no retry because the order is now paid.
findings.suggested_fix: Await these (Promise.allSettled with a short timeout) before responding, or enqueue them durably (automation_jobs row inside/next to the settle) so a frozen function can't lose them.
findings.reason: earnPointsForOrder, triggerSettlementMessage, triggerDueBillMessage and scheduleFeedbackForOrder are started with .catch() only, and res.json(order) follows immediately (routes.ts ~2777-2798). CLAUDE.md documents that Vercel can freeze the function after the response, and the conditional settle means these one-time effects never re-run. Not documented as intended.

findings.title: move-table doesn't verify the target table is free or the order still active; overwrites another order's table assignment
findings.detail: updateOrder sets the new tableId and updateTableStatus(newTableId,'running',id) unconditionally. The client offers only tables that were free when the dialog's query ran (staleTime 0 but no lock), so two staff moving onto the same table, or a stale list, lands two orders on one table; a paid/cancelled order can also be moved onto a free table and mark it running. newTableId is not coerced/validated (string or nonexistent id accepted).
findings.failure_scenario: Two waiters each open Move Table and pick table 7 within seconds. The second move sets table 7's currentOrderId to its order; the first order still has tableId 7 but is no longer the table's current order and disappears from the Tables card.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a conditional UPDATE tables SET ... WHERE id=$new AND status='free' and 409 when 0 rows; require the order to be unpaid and not cancelled; validate newTableId as a positive integer.
findings.reason: move-table (routes.ts 3177-3212) writes order.tableId and sets the new table to running unconditionally, with no check that the table is free, no check of order state, and no validation of newTableId. The defect is real, but it needs two managers racing (both holding PIN elevation) or a direct call, so it is rated low.

findings.title: Print-on-table-move bypasses the print pipeline: getSettings() fallback, direct sendToPrinter after res.json, no print_jobs bridge
findings.detail: The KOT after a move is built and sent fire-and-forget after the response, straight to sendToPrinter with getSettings() (CLAUDE.md: any code that picks a printer must use getLiveSettings()). On Vercel the function may be frozen post-response and cannot reach a LAN/USB printer anyway, because it never creates a print_jobs row for the desktop bridge; failures are only console.warn'd. It also has no KOT number and defaults width to 32 instead of the printer's 48-col default used elsewhere.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner enables 'Print KOT on table move' with the kitchen printer on the Electron host. Staff move table 3 -> 8 from a phone (Vercel): no ticket ever prints and nobody is told, so the kitchen keeps sending food to table 3.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the move KOT through runKotPrint/dispatchRemotePrintJobs (print_jobs + PRINT_JOB broadcast) using getLiveSettings(), and await it (or at least the job insert) before responding.
findings.reason: The print-on-move block (routes.ts 3214-3243) runs after res.json and uses getSettings() instead of getLiveSettings(), contrary to CLAUDE.md's rule for picking a printer. It calls sendToPrinter directly with no print_jobs row or PRINT_JOB broadcast, so a printer on the Electron host is never reached from Vercel. It defaults the width to 32 and only console.warns on failure.

findings.title: Merge drops the source order's discount — merged bill is higher than the two bills it replaced
findings.detail: computeTotalsFromLines gets only targetOrder.discountAmount. The source's container and delivery charges are summed (the 'aggregate-neutral' rule CLAUDE.md describes for merge), but the source discount is silently discarded and the source order deleted.
findings.failure_scenario: Table 2 (₹1,000, manager-approved ₹100 discount) is merged into table 5 (₹800, no discount) at 5% tax. Before: 945 + 840 = ₹1,785. After merge: (1,800 − 0)×1.05 = ₹1,890 — the customer is billed ₹105 more and the approved discount leaves no trace on the surviving order.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass targetDiscount + sourceDiscount (clamped to the combined subtotal) and persist discountAmount in targetTotals.
findings.reason: computeTotalsFromLines receives only targetOrder.discountAmount (routes.ts ~3273), while the container and delivery charges from both orders are summed. targetTotals omits discountAmount, and the source order is then deleted, so its stored discount is lost and the merged total is higher than the two bills combined. CLAUDE.md describes merge as aggregate-neutral, and this breaks that.

findings.title: Off-site backup omits restaurant_settings and the HR/print/conversation tables
findings.detail: dumpAllTables() exports 29 tables but not restaurant_settings (tax rate, printers, GST, bill/KOT counters — CLAUDE.md's single source of truth), staff_profiles (salaries/biometric ids), attendance, leaves, shifts, shift_assignments, conversations, conversation_messages or print_jobs.
findings.failure_scenario: The DB is lost and restored from the R2 backup: orders restore, but the tax rate/printer/counter settings are gone (the app 503s on settings until rebuilt by hand, and bill numbers restart and collide with restored orders' UNIQUE orderNumber), and all attendance/leave/salary history is unrecoverable.
findings.suggested_fix: Dump every table in shared/schema.ts (derive the list from the schema exports rather than a hand-maintained list) and add a check that fails the backup when a schema table is missing.
findings.reason: dumpAllTables (backupService.ts 48-90) lists 29 tables. shared/schema.ts defines 38, and the list omits restaurant_settings, print_jobs, conversations, conversation_messages, staff_profiles, attendance, leaves, shifts and shift_assignments. runBackup is scheduled by dailyScheduler.ts and exposed in routes.ts.

findings.title: Birthday/anniversary wishes bypass the WhatsApp driver: with Baileys they are dry-run yet recorded as 'sent'
findings.detail: runBirthdayAutomation uses sendWhatsAppMessage (Meta/WATI only). On a restaurant using the Baileys driver with neither Meta nor WATI keys, it returns {success:true, mode:'dry_run'}; the job is inserted with status 'sent', the coupon is issued, and alreadySentToday blocks any retry. It also skips the opt-out file (isOptedOut), maxPerDay and the outbound queue's pacing that every other path goes through (CLAUDE.md: messagingService sends driver-first).
findings.failure_scenario: Owner pairs WhatsApp via Baileys and turns on birthday automation. Every birthday customer gets a BDAY coupon created but never receives any message; automation_jobs shows BIRTHDAY 'sent'.
findings.suggested_fix: Send through enqueueWhatsApp/messagingService (driver-first, queue, maxPerDay, opt-out), and record dry_run as status 'dry_run'/'skipped', not 'sent'.
findings.reason: The cited line is wrong (the file has 203 lines; the code is at 160-171), but the behaviour is confirmed. runBirthdayAutomation calls whatsappService.sendWhatsAppMessage, which uses Meta, then WATI, and otherwise falls back to {success:true, mode:'dry_run'}. The job is then inserted with status 'sent' because result.success is true, and alreadySentToday blocks a retry. The Baileys driver, the outbound queue and maxPerDay are never used.

findings.title: POST /api/crm/segment/batch is shadowed by POST /api/crm/segment/:key (registered first)
findings.detail: Express matches routes in registration order, so 'batch' is captured as :key by the requireAuth single-customer handler; the requireAdmin batch handler is unreachable.
findings.failure_scenario: An admin calls the batch segmentation endpoint: it runs runSegmentationForCustomer('batch','batch') (possibly creating a bogus customer) and returns ok, while no customer is actually re-segmented.
findings.reason: POST /api/crm/segment/:key (routes.ts 4033) is registered before POST /api/crm/segment/batch (4052), so Express matches 'batch' as :key. The admin batch handler is unreachable.

findings.title: Payment route hand-rolls settlement math and accepts arbitrary method labels instead of resolveSettlement + cash/UPI validation
findings.detail: resolveSettlement and SETTLE_TOLERANCE are imported but only the tolerance is used; breakdown keys are whatever p.method/paymentMethod the client sends (Billing still offers card/online). shared/paymentSplit and Reports/Tables tiles only show cash and upi, so such money is counted in Sales but in neither Cash nor UPI. CLAUDE.md explicitly says never hand-roll this comparison again; settle-due already validates methods (bad_method).
findings.failure_scenario: A settle with payments:[{method:'card',amount:500}] (or Billing's Card option) is recorded as paid ₹500: Tables 'Sales ₹T' includes it but Cash + UPI no longer add up to Sales, and Reports -> Payments shows the ₹500 nowhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Build cash/upi from payments, reject any other method (400 bad_method) on the rich path, and call resolveSettlement({mode, cash, upi, orderTotal}) for paid/change/shortfall.
findings.reason: The rich path builds the breakdown from any p.method, and the legacy path uses paymentMethod verbatim. Billing.tsx still offers card and online (lines 694 and 696). collectedByMethod then keys the money under 'card', which the Cash/UPI-only tiles never show. resolveSettlement is imported but unused, and the hand-rolled math is numerically equivalent, so the only real effect is unreported money from the label.

findings.title: items_edit audit compares the stored (2-dp) total against the unrounded priced.total, logging spurious 'Bill Modified' rows
findings.detail: totalBefore is parsed from the stored toFixed(2) string, totalAfter is the raw float (e.g. 690.795). Any non-noop save whose items/money didn't change (customer name, instructions, parcel note) yields moneyChanged=true and an order.items_edit row with totalBefore 690.8 vs totalAfter 690.795; the SQL classifier then counts it as Bill Modified.
findings.failure_scenario: Staff adds a customer phone to a running table's order: Reports -> KOT & Bill Activity shows a 'Bill Modified' event although the bill is identical.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare against Number(totals.totalAmount) (the persisted rounded value) for totalAfter and the other money fields.
findings.reason: totalBefore is parsed from the stored 2-dp string, while totalAfter is priced.total, which computeTotals returns unrounded (taxable + tax + charges, orderPricing.ts:144). A changed-but-money-identical save (customer name, notes or parcel flag) makes moneyChanged true and logs an items_edit row, which classifyItemsEditRow counts as Bill Modified.

findings.title: Attendance report / recompute-shifts default month and /api/attendance/today use UTC dates; roster default week uses the old wrong formula
findings.detail: new Date().toISOString().slice(0,7) and storage.getTodayAttendance's toISOString date are UTC; between 00:00 and 05:30 IST on the 1st they return the previous month/day. The /api/shifts/roster fallback week still uses the Math.ceil(startOfYear...) formula CLAUDE.md says was replaced by shared/weekMath.ts. Attendance import also turns non-ISO date strings into dates via local-midnight toISOString, shifting them one day back on an IST host.
findings.failure_scenario: On an Electron host in IST, importing a sheet with dates like '11/04/2026' stores every row on 2026-11-03; at 00:30 IST on the 1st, the Today board shows yesterday's punches.
findings.suggested_fix: Use istCalendarDate()/weekStringOf() from the shared helpers and parse import dates by their components, not via toISOString.
findings.reason: /api/attendance/report and recompute-shifts default the month with toISOString().slice(0,7), which is UTC. getTodayAttendance uses a UTC toISOString date. The roster fallback week (routes.ts 4473-4474) still uses the old Math.ceil(startOfYear) formula that CLAUDE.md says was replaced by weekMath. The import parses non-ISO dates with new Date() then toISOString, which shifts them one day earlier on an IST host. All of these are real.

findings.title: Automation logs, stats and customer prefs are readable/writable by any session
findings.detail: GET /api/automation/logs and /prefs and POST /api/automation/prefs/:customerId are requireAuth, while config/run/clear are admin. Logs contain every customer's phone and message text.
findings.failure_scenario: A staff PIN session downloads 2,000 customer phone numbers with message history, or flips a customer's doNotSend/mutedUntil.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate these with requireManagerOrAdmin (or requireAdmin like /api/automation/config).
findings.reason: GET /api/automation/logs and /stats, and POST/GET /api/automation/prefs, are requireAuth (routes.ts 3755, 3772, 3787, 3795), while config, run and log clear are requireAdmin. A staff session can read message logs and toggle a customer's doNotSend. Customer phones are already visible to staff in other places (the POS directory), so this is rated low.
